messages.content:
Hi there! Thanks for taking the time to talk with me today about the student portal enhancements. I'm really looking forward to understanding what you're hoping to achieve with the personalised timetable management, grade notifications, and module feedback system. 

To start off, could you tell me what the high-level goals are for enhancing the portal? What are you hoping to improve for the students?

Hey! Thanks for having me. So, honestly, I just want the timetable to be way easier to read and use. Right now, it’s kind of a mess, and it’s hard to keep track of everything. I think if I could colour-code my modules or hide classes that got cancelled, that would help a lot. 

Also, I really want to get notified right away when grades come out. It’s super annoying to keep checking all the time. And, feedback on modules—there should be an easy way to give my thoughts after classes wrap up. It would be nice to know that what I say is actually heard, you know? So yeah, that’s pretty much it!

Thanks for sharing that! It sounds like you’re looking for a more user-friendly timetable, with features like colour-coding and the ability to hide cancelled classes. 

For the grade notifications, you mentioned wanting to be notified right away when grades are released. Can you tell me a bit more about how you'd like that notification process to work? Would you prefer email alerts, app notifications, or something else?

Yeah, definitely! I think it would be cool to get notifications on my phone or through the app. I don’t always check my email, so if I could get a pop-up or something on my phone, that would be awesome. Just something that lets me know right away, you know? It gets really stressful waiting for grades, so having that reminder would help a lot!

Got it! So you'd like to receive pop-up notifications on your phone or through the app to alert you right away when grades are available. That sounds like a great way to ease the stress of waiting for grades!

Now, regarding the module feedback system, you mentioned wanting an easy way to give your thoughts after classes. Can you describe what you envision for that? Like, what kind of questions or areas would you want to provide feedback on?

Hmm, I guess I’d just want to share my thoughts on how the module went overall. Like, was the content good? Did the teacher explain things well? And maybe if the resources were helpful or not. Just stuff that would help make the course better for next time. It would be nice to have a simple way to do that right after the term ends, so it’s fresh in my mind. I’m not sure about specific questions, but just a chance to say what I think would be great!

Thanks for that! So you’d like the module feedback system to allow you to share your overall thoughts on the module, including the content quality, the teacher's explanations, and the helpfulness of the resources. A simple way to provide that feedback right after the term ends would be ideal for you. 

To wrap things up, are there any limitations or restrictions we should consider while implementing these enhancements, like technical constraints or anything else?

Oh, I haven't really thought about that. I just know what I want to see improved. I guess it’s up to the tech people to figure out how to make it happen, right? I'm just really focused on making it easier for us students to use!

That makes sense! You're mainly focused on the improvements and leaving the technical details to the experts. 

So just to recap what we've discussed: 

1. You want a personalised timetable that allows for colour-coding and hiding cancelled classes.
2. You’d like to receive pop-up notifications on your phone or through the app when grades are released.
3. You want a module feedback system that lets you share your overall thoughts on the module, including the content, teaching, and resources.
4. You prefer this feedback system to be available right after the term ends so that your thoughts are fresh.
5. You're not concerned with the technical limitations, focusing instead on the user experience.

If that’s correct, I think we have a clear set of requirements! 

So, I’ll just say... 

REQUIREMENTS_COMPLETE
